title: noisy-tenant-starvation-hypothesis-logbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick working log for the set of small but repeated degradations we observed in dedicated GPU pools during the 2024-10 spike. This is intentionally informal — capture hypotheses, short experiments, and next-step runbook edits so we can converge on durable mitigations.

Executive summary (short):
- Symptoms: intermittent multi-minute request stalls for customers on Dedicated pools A/B causing p99 tail latency to jump 3-8x for several tenants between 02:00-05:00 UTC on high-traffic days.
- Impact: concentrated on 4 customers (IDs masked) running large context length generation; affected ~2-7% of requests across the pool during windows, overall capacity nominal. No node OOMs, no host-level GPU faults.
- Working hypothesis: noisy-tenant starvation — aggressive KV-cache churn + large-batch workloads triggered autoscaler and eviction interactions that temporarily starved small/medium tenants. Secondary hypothesis: autoscaler cooldown misconfig allowed scale-down while long-running sequences were still consuming ephemeral slots.

Signals we saw (metrics and logs):
- p99 token-serv latency per-pool: baseline 220ms -> observed spikes to 1.6s during incidents.
- GPU util: steady 60-75% across pool (no overall saturation) but per-instance GPU util showed oscillation patterns indicative of busy/idle cycles.
- Pod queue depth (requests waiting per-worker): bursts to 180% of expected queue targets for 4-6 minutes.
- Eviction logs: repeated ephemeral-worker evict attempts (pod eviction reason: NodePressure not present; eviction surfaced from autoscaler-driven reclaim).
- KV cache miss rate: increased by ~30% for tenant-correlated keys when burst begins.
- Trace samples: tail traces show long tail on first-token of new sequences (KV warm-up).

Timeline (abridged):
- 2024-10-28 01:47 UTC — first customer alert (high latencies). Oncall routed to SRE.
- 01:50 — observed p99 spike; opened incident channel.
- 01:53 — confirmed not hardware (no GPU ECC or driver errors).
- 02:05 — noticed higher eviction count and autoscale events in pool-A: scale-down at 01:58 then a quick scale-up at 02:02.
- 02:12 — isolated tenant set by temporarily moving two noisy jobs to quarantine pool; latency for victims improved within 90s.
- 02:40 — reverted quarantine while we drafted mitigation; incident recurred at 04:03 with similar pattern.

Initial experiments run (short notes):
1) Isolate noisy tenants
   - Action: move suspected noisy jobs (large batch gen) to quarantine pool with hard concurrency cap=1.
   - Result: victim tenant latency improved rapidly; noisy tenant still produced KV-churn but contained.

2) Increase autoscaler min replicas for pool-A to avoid scale-down
   - Action: bump minReplicas + increase scale-down cooldown to 8m.
   - Result: fewer rapid scale-down/up cycles. Latency spikes decreased but not eliminated (some spikes attributable to per-instance cache thrash).

3) Add per-tenant request cap at the gateway for heavy-context requests
   - Action: add temporary rate-limit for large-context paths for tenants showing >x concurrent seqs.
   - Result: immediate improvement in tail; causes cost/throughput tradeoff — flagged to product.

Runbook draft (triage checklist for similar incidents):
- Step 0: Acknowledge incident: create #inc channel with pool and tenant tags.
- Step 1: Observe metrics to classify: is p99 latency pool-wide or tenant-scoped? (query: pool.p99_token_latency / pool.per_tenant_p99).
- Step 2: Check host/GPU health (nvidia-smi errors, node reboot logs) — if yes, escalates to infra-hardware path.
- Step 3: Check autoscaler events in last 10m (k8s HorizontalPodAutoscaler / custom scaler logs). If scale-down/up happened within 5m window, suspect eviction interaction.
- Step 4: Check eviction+pod-restart patterns and pod scheduling (kubectl get events -n inference): any pods terminated around incident?
- Step 5: Pull KV cache hit-rate per-tenant; if miss-rate > 20% increase correlated with spike, mark "cache-thrash".
- Step 6: Quick mitigation options (pick one or more):
    a) Migrate suspected noisy tenant(s) to quarantine pool (note: coordinate with infra to avoid cross-tenant data leak).
    b) Increase pool minReplicas and extend scale-down cooldown (temporary).
    c) Apply per-tenant concurrency cap / large-context rate-limit.
    d) Roll out a graceful fallback model (smaller context) for affected tenants if available.
- Step 7: If mitigations do not improve in 5-10 minutes, consider global throttling or emergency maintenance (announce to customers).
- Step 8: Collect traces and attach to Jira incident; preserve logs and set retention.

Interesting notes and questions (notes-to-self style):
- Why do we see per-instance oscillations with pool-level GPU util moderate? Possibly skewed distribution of sequence lengths per-worker or scheduling packing that leaves small hot shards. Need per-worker sequence length histogram.
- Autoscaler behavior: In one observed window scale-down occurred while there were inflight long sequences; scale-down attempted to reclaim ephemeral workers which caused increased queueing. Need to consider an in-flight-buffered-cooldown or in-flight-aware scaling.
- KV cache eviction policy: LRU across tenants may be too coarse; consider tenant-aware pinning for large context model keys.

Suggested durable mitigations (higher confidence):
- Implement per-tenant soft reservations: a small guaranteed slot count for heavy customers to avoid eviction cascade. (Owner: Jonah)
- Autoscaler change: add in-flight-request guard that prevents scale-down if #inflight_long_seq > threshold. (Owner: Marisol)
- Instrumentation: add per-worker seq-length distribution and per-tenant KV cache churn metric (Owner: Ethan).

Lower-confidence ideas to explore:
- Model-level cache partitioning (logical shards per-tenant) or tenant-aware KV namespaces. Tradeoffs: memory footprint, complexity.
- Smarter packer that balances long-running sequences across nodes to avoid localized starvation.

Follow-ups / action items (owners + dates):
- SRE-842 (Jonah) — design doc for per-tenant soft reservations; due 2024-11-20.
- SRE-843 (Marisol) — prototype in-flight aware autoscaler logic (simulator + canary) due 2024-12-03.
- Observability spike (Ethan) — add new Grafana dashboard with per-worker sequence histograms and KV-churn; due 2024-11-15.
- Product sync — discuss per-tenant rate limits + customer impact (Asha) — schedule 11/13.

Short-term playbook edits to commit after incident closes:
- Add a new incident tag "noisy-tenant" and include quick links to quarantine pool creation steps.
- Add explicit checklist: before scaling pool down, check "inflight long sequences" metric.
- Create quick query snippets for oncall:
    - pool p99: metrics.query("pool.token_latency_percentile{percentile=99, pool="pool-A"}")
    - per-tenant kv miss: metrics.query("kv_cache.miss_rate{tenant=~"customer-.*"}")

Customer communication notes (draft language):
- "We observed transient degradation in request latency in a subset of dedicated GPU pools due to resource contention triggered by bursty large-context workloads. We contained the impact and have implemented short-term mitigations; our engineering team is working on architectural fixes (in-flight-aware scaling and tenant reservations) to prevent recurrence. We will follow up with timelines for fixes."

Open questions to discuss in postmortem:
- Should Dedicated pools expose a per-tenant SLAs? If yes, how to implement without sacrificing bin-packing efficiency?
- What cost delta do we accept for guaranteed reservations?
- Is tenant-aware KV namespaces feasible given model loader semantics and serving runtime constraints?

Appendix: useful commands (oncall crib sheet)
- Move pod to quarantine (example): kubectl cordon node-x; annotate pods with pool=quarantine; scale deployment --replicas=2 --namespace=inference
- Increase minReplicas: kubectl patch hpa pool-a-hpa -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}' -n inference
- Query autoscaler events: kubectl get events -n kube-system --field-selector involvedObject.name=pool-a-autoscaler

Raw log snippets (redacted):
- "evicting pod worker-572 reason=ScaleDownTTL owner=autoscaler"
- "tenant=customer-42 kv.miss=0.61 -> high"

Notes to future self:
- When reproducing: synthesize workload with mixture of 1) large-context long-lived sequences, 2) short bursty queries — we want to stress cache churn without saturating GPU. Use the infra-loadkit script `loadkit/gpu/starve_test.py` (WIP) and iterate.

End of log.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-06 initial notes (Asha)
- 2024-11-08 ran isolation experiment and recorded results (Jonah)
- 2024-11-12 added action items and ownerships after server sync (Marisol)
